explanations.answer: The time has not yet come
explanations.explanation: That's the line. God says, “These people say, ‘The time has not yet come to rebuild the house of the LORD.’” It's all about timing. I've said "I'll get to it later" so many times that "later" should have my mailing address.

explanations.answer: The work is too hard for us
explanations.explanation: I can see why that one sounds believable, friend. But the words God quotes aren't about the work being hard. They say, “The time has not yet come to rebuild the house of the LORD.” The people's complaint is about the calendar.

explanations.answer: We have no stones to build with
explanations.explanation: Stones never come up in what the people say. The words God repeats are, “The time has not yet come to rebuild the house of the LORD.” The building material God names later is lumber: “Go up into the hills, bring down lumber, and build the house…”

explanations.answer: Living in paneled houses while His house lies in ruins
explanations.explanation: Yes, that's the question. God asks, “Is it a time for you yourselves to live in your paneled houses, while this house lies in ruins?” Paneled houses are the nice kind, with the fancy wall covering. God puts those cozy homes right next to His house lying in ruins.

explanations.answer: Guarding their own walls while His gates stand open
explanations.explanation: That sounds like a strong picture, but walls and gates aren't in God's question. He asks about their paneled houses and about this house lying in ruins. The question sets their homes next to His house, and that's it.

explanations.answer: Buying new fields while His priests go without
explanations.explanation: Fields and priests aren't in this question at all, friend. God asks, “Is it a time for you yourselves to live in your paneled houses, while this house lies in ruins?” The first thing He points to is their paneled houses.

Careful, friend, that last word flips it. God says, “You have planted much but harvested little.” So they planted a lot, but the harvest came up small. It's like putting in a huge cookie order and getting a few crumbs back.
You caught the flip. God says, “You have planted much but harvested little.” They did plant a lot, but the harvest was small.
It's the opposite, friend. God says, “You put on clothes but never get warm.” So they get dressed, and the chill stays right there with them. Sweater on, still shivering.
That's right. God says, “You put on clothes but never get warm.” They put the clothes on, but they still don't get warm. A coat that doesn't help is just a heavy hanger with arms.

explanations.answer: Their money keeps slipping away from them
explanations.explanation: That's the picture. A bag pierced through has a hole in it, so whatever goes in doesn't stay. They keep earning wages, and the wages keep leaking out the bottom. It's like carrying a box of cookies with a tear in it and leaving a trail of crumbs all the way home.

explanations.answer: Thieves keep breaking in and taking their money
explanations.explanation: Nobody is breaking in here, friend. God says the wages go into “a bag pierced through.” The problem is a hole in the bag, and the text doesn't mention any thief.

explanations.answer: They hide their money away and forget about it
explanations.explanation: Hiding and forgetting isn't in the text. God says, “You earn wages to put into a bag pierced through.” The picture is a bag with a hole in it, so the money doesn't stay put.

explanations.answer: So He may take pleasure in it and be glorified
explanations.explanation: That's what God says. He tells them to build the house “so that I may take pleasure in it and be glorified, says the LORD.” The reason God gives is about Himself and His house. And He doesn't ask them to wait until the timing feels right first.

explanations.answer: So the priests can live in it and be safe
explanations.explanation: Priests living in it and being safe isn't part of what God says. He gives His reason: “so that I may take pleasure in it and be glorified, says the LORD.” The house is for Him.

explanations.answer: So the governor can rule from it in peace
explanations.explanation: Zerubbabel is the governor of Judah, and God does speak to him in verse 1. But the reason God gives for building has nothing to do with ruling. He says, “so that I may take pleasure in it and be glorified, says the LORD.”

True, and God says it plainly: “And what you brought home, I blew away.” So the little they did bring home didn't stay either. It's like carrying a tray of fresh cookies in from the kitchen and having a gust of wind take half of them.
It's true, friend. God says it Himself: “And what you brought home, I blew away.” The words come right from the LORD of Hosts.

Yes. God says, “Therefore, on account of you the heavens have withheld their dew and the earth has withheld its crops.” The dew stays up in the sky, and the crops stay in the ground. Two things held back at once.
It is true, friend. God says, “Therefore, on account of you the heavens have withheld their dew and the earth has withheld its crops.” The dew is held back, and the crops are held back with it.
Yes, drought. God says, “I have summoned a drought on the fields and on the mountains…” Remember, He had also said the heavens had withheld their dew. Fields and mountains are both in it.

Close in size, but that's the other direction. God says, “I have summoned a drought on the fields and on the mountains…” A drought is a dry stretch, and a flood is the opposite. The dew being withheld in verse 10 fits the dry picture.
Frost sounds like it could cut a crop down, friend. But the word God uses is drought: “I have summoned a drought on the fields and on the mountains…” Frost doesn't show up anywhere in these verses.
No animal gets a pass here. God says the drought is “on man and beast, and on all the labor of your hands.” So beasts are named right alongside people. Nobody on the farm is left out.
That's right. God says He has summoned the drought “on man and beast, and on all the labor of your hands.” The animals are named in it, not skipped over.
